title: Embed compatibility facade: stable cursor semantics, transient-error mapping, and stream-safe embeddings responses
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Deliver a compatibility facade for embeddings and rerank endpoints that normalizes cursor semantics, maps transient internal errors to stable client-facing HTTP codes, and ensures streaming responses and function-calling flows remain backwards compatible for legacy clients.
problem_statement: Multiple customers and legacy SDKs expect stable 'cursor' semantics and consistent HTTP errors when interacting with embeddings and rerank endpoints. Recent runtime changes (continuous batching + KV cache) introduced subtle non-idempotent behavior in cursor generation and exposed internal transient errors (e.g., 502/504) that upstream clients retry in unsafe ways. Streaming/partial responses for embed-rerank combos also changed framing, breaking some client's parsers.
goals: Define a single cursor contract that covers page tokens, expiration, and deterministic reconstruction for popular SDK versions
Map internal transient/runtime errors to a normalized set of client-facing codes with clear retry semantics
Provide a thin facade shim in the API gateway that preserves streaming chunk framing expected by legacy clients
Ship tests and a migration playbook for partner integrators and support to reduce post-release incidents
out_of_scope: Full refactor of the runtime KV cache; large-scale schema changes to embeddings payloads
acceptance_criteria: Cursor token format v1 is documented and validated by unit/integration tests; SDKs can round-trip page tokens up to 1000 items
A mapping table for internal error classes -> client HTTP codes exists and is deployed (e.g., transient worker OOM -> 429 with Retry-After, upstream connection reset -> 502 with non-retry guidance)
Streaming responses for embed+rerrank preserve chunk boundaries for legacy clients when 'compat_level=legacy' header is present
Rollout is staged: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback on regression metrics defined in runbook
implementation_notes: Work split between gateway shim (stateless token normalization), runtime adapters (idempotent cursor emission), and SDK acceptance tests. Use a deterministic HMAC with short TTL for cursor tokens to allow stateless validation in the gateway. Add telemetry tags to track cursor rejections and fallbacks.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: HMAC key rotation could invalidate cursors. Mitigation: support multiple active keys and implement smooth key rollover in gateway
Risk: Overmapping errors might hide actionable signals from customers. Mitigation: include original error details in internal logs and provide guidance in 4xx/5xx body for enterprise customers
Risk: Streaming shim could add latency. Mitigation: microbenchmark shim (<1ms median added) and gate behind rollout flag
notes: We discussed two cursor designs: an opaque HMAC token vs structured JSON cursor. Chosen approach: opaque HMAC containing minimal metadata (offset, model-id, ttl) to preserve future flexibility and prevent clients from depending on internals.
design_feedback: Design reviewed by UX and Engineering on 2026-02-28. PM asked for explicit compatibility header to let clients opt into legacy framing; engineering requested a fallthrough path for unknown cursors.
qa_plan: Create regression suite that exercises: cursor round-trip, mismatched-model cursors, expired cursors, simulated transient errors (connection reset, worker timeout), and streaming chunk reassembly under legacy header. Automate in nightly runs and include a synthetic traffic canary.
rollout_plan: Deploy facade behind feature flag. Stage traffic 0% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours with SLO and error budget checks. Run a 72-hour canary with concierge monitoring for partner accounts.
